design_decisions.question: How to represent derivation provenance natively without redesigning Atlas's identity model?
design_decisions.decision: Additive fields only: ConstraintCheckDerivation is a new type; ConstraintResult gains a derivation: Vec<ConstraintCheckDerivation> field. No change to SemanticRecordId/SemanticRecordHeader, no new identity scheme -- confirmed by the R5 synthesis record's own finding (Atlas's existing identity/evidence split already structurally fits this pattern) and verified directly against the real evaluate_constraints/ConstraintResult types before implementing.

design_decisions.question: How does derivation provenance reach the engineering graph, given SemanticFact (the existing lossy compatibility envelope) has no room for structured per-check provenance?
design_decisions.decision: A new, dedicated add_constraint_derivations function, mirroring add_dependency_closure's established precedent exactly: a typed report projects itself directly into the graph, bypassing the SemanticFact envelope entirely. One ConstraintResult node per result; a SUPPORTED_BY edge to every DeclaredNode graph node an AttributeEquals check consulted, reusing the SAME declared_node_id scheme the existing DeclaredNode projection arm already uses so both converge on one node rather than diverging.
